title.narrative: A tool for systematic reporting of members on provision of movement and access information

description.narrative: A tool for systematic reporting of members on provision of movement and access information

comment.narrative: No such tool yet exists within AIDA
One data tracking and analysis tool on access and movement developed and employed by AIDA secretariat be end of project

A tool as was envisioned at the inception of the action was never fully materialized on and there were particular elements that were being stood up by ASU on a proprietary platform. AIDA made the determination that it would be redundant to create its own platform and therefore shifted its efforts into building up complimentary tracking tools such as an international staff tracking tool for Gaza which proved to be extremely helpful in the escalations of 2022 and 2023. AIDA needs to look more at tool visualization moving on successive projects. It collects reams of data but needs to be able to present them in a way that is visually captivating and tells a compelling story at the same time.

title.narrative: key external stakeholders (diplomatic, UN, and donor) referencing or reflecting AIDA advocacy priorities and positions in their own policy documents, public communications, SOPs and practices.

description.narrative: key external stakeholders (diplomatic, UN, and donor) referencing or reflecting AIDA advocacy priorities and positions in their own policy documents, public communications, SOPs and practices.

comment.narrative: AIDA has averaged an uptake adoption of 23 positionspolicy statement by external actors per annum in years past. These are reflected at different levels within the respective organizations and most often at the local level Palestine. However it has been some time since AIDA collected information on this type of indicator and therefore starting from a zero baseline.

AIDA positions were taken into consideration for both internal UN communiques on Access and Movement primarily from the UNHCT and in public statements. This was particularly true on the positions regarding CTL Designations of the Palestinian NGOs by Israel the process and mechanisms that INGOs currently employ to mitigate aid diversion in Gaza the access of Palestinian humanitarian workers in and out of Gaza and the call to desist with the provisions of the COGAT West Bank Foreigners Residency policy. Many of these points were underlined in the AIDA Quarterly Aid Obstruction bulletins.

title.narrative: Operational regulations or compliance policies issued by duty bearers that are revised, or positively influenced by AIDAs advocacy.

description.narrative: Operational regulations or compliance policies issued by duty bearers that are revised, or positively influenced by AIDAs advocacy.

comment.narrative: On average AIDA will aim to influence at least one significant operational policy per year.

DFA discarded policy change limiting term of months an intl staff could stay in Gaza. MoIGoI continued to process INGO B1 visas after arrival in country despite COGAT seeking to change to a more cumbersome system. In addition to these there was the reversal of policy enforcement on foreign residency restrictions in the West Bank from COGAT. AIDA also was able to successfully influence positive outcomes for INGOs regarding increased measures to levy more barriers on aid being considered by UK donors.
